passage:
A warehouse used robots to move shelves of products to workers. Orders became faster, but the work also changed.
Workers no longer walked long distances. Instead, they stood at stations and picked items from shelves brought by robots. Some liked being less tired. Others found the repeated motions stressful.
A reporter interviewed workers, managers, and safety experts. The article showed no simple answer.
Automation can reduce some burdens while creating others.
The warehouse became a case study in modern labor. When machines enter a workplace, people should ask not only how much faster work becomes, but what kind of work humans are left to do.
